package.name: WebAir Travel Agent
package.description: Search WebAir flights, explain fare rules, prepare a booking quote and simulate a purchase through WebAir's own semantic API, using a travel profile, a passenger identity and a payment method that the person's host owns and grants per run. WebAir publishes the behavior; the person's runtime supplies the authority. WebAir is a fictional demo airline: nothing is ever booked or charged.

tools.description: WebAir semantic API: price, baggage allowance, change and refund policy of one fare returned by a search.

Host-owned resource: the one passenger identity the person granted for this run. It takes no arguments, so the package cannot name or enumerate the host's resources; the host returns the granted one or refuses.

Host-owned resource: the one travel profile the person granted for this run. It takes no arguments, so the package cannot name or enumerate the host's resources; the host returns the granted one or refuses.

WebAir semantic API: quote one fare for the passenger identity the person granted for this run, supplied by the host and sent to WebAir only in this call. Reserves nothing, stores nothing, charges nothing.

WebAir semantic API: search fictional WebAir flights for one route and date, optionally nonstop, by cabin or under a per-passenger price. A refusal (invalid route, date outside the schedule) is returned as data.

WebAir semantic API: simulate paying one exact quote for the granted passenger, with the payment method the person granted (an opaque demo identifier supplied by the host). Fictional: no real transaction ever occurs and nothing is charged. Requires the separate purchase permission, so search or quote authority can never become purchase authority.

Host-owned resource: the one payment method the person granted for this run. It takes no arguments, so the package cannot name or enumerate the host's resources; the host returns the granted one or refuses.

booking.description: Ask WebAir for a booking quote of the fare the workflow selects, for the passenger identity you grant. Nothing is reserved or charged.

purchase.description: Leave both empty, or authorize one simulated purchase: the exact quote id and fare id an earlier quote returned. Needs the passenger identity that quote was made for, a payment method and the purchase permission.

request.description: The person's travel request in their own words, for example: Find me a flight to Zurich on 9 October under $900.

input.note: The package's own declared input schema. The runner validates every run against it again before any instruction reaches a model.

task.prompt: Where would you like to fly with WebAir?

booking.label: Prepare a booking quote for the passenger I grant

request.placeholder: Find me a flight to Zurich on 9 October under $900.

nodes.check-quote-offer: Check the quote against the search

permissions.description: Call WebAir's semantic API (a fictional demo airline): search flights, read fare rules, request a booking quote and, only with the separate purchase permission, simulate a purchase.

Read the travel profile you choose (home airport, preferred cabin, nonstop preference) when a request leaves those unstated. The profile becomes search criteria sent to WebAir; it is never shown to a model as a profile.
Read the passenger identity you choose (name and contact email) and send it to WebAir for a booking quote or a simulated purchase, and nowhere else. No model sees it.

Read which payment method you choose (an opaque demo identifier and a display label, never a card number) and send the identifier to WebAir with a simulated purchase, and nowhere else. No model sees it.

Simulate purchasing the one exact quote a task names, with the payment method you choose. Fictional: WebAir performs no real transaction and charges nothing. Consequential by design: grant it once, for one run.
Use the host-selected model router to interpret the request, choose fares and write the answer.
Read and write explicit worker state views for this run only.
